Cases of abdominal pain, vomiting, loose motion, headache and fever were reported from Village Ratka Farm, No 3 Rajakhana, Sub-District Jonai, District Dhemaji. Cases were treated symptomatically. 3 rectal swabs collected and sent to AMCH Dibrugarh tested positive for Salmonella enterica by culture. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of loose motions and vomiting were reported from Village Tingrai Doom Gaon No.2, Sub-District Naharkatiya, District Dibrugarh. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 10 to 45 years. Cases consumed prasad at a funeral ceremony. 1 rectal swab sample was collected from an affected person for culture and was sent to the State Referral Laboratory (SRL), Department of Microbiology, Assam Medical College and Hospital (AMCH) and it was negative. 2 water samples collected from the water used for soaking the Prasad ingredients were tested. Both showed a presumptive coliform count >180 bacilli/100ml of water, and were unsatisfactory for drinking purpose. Cases were treated at Sassoni CHC and Naharkatia SDCH. Chlorination of water sources done. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of nausea, fever, vomiting and diarrhea were reported from Village Haribhanga, Sub-District Samaguri, District Nagaon. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 4 to 60 years. Cases had consumed prashad at a religious ceremony. In this food poisoning incident, a 47 year-old female case expired on 19/09/2026. 7 stool samples were tested by culture at the Microbiology Department, NMCH, Nagaon, and showed growth of non- typhoidal Salmonella species after 24 hours of aerobic incubation at 37°C. 2 water samples were tested at DPHL, IDSP, Nagaon, and both were classified as Class IV (unfit for drinking) based on the presumptive coliform count (MPN). The cases were treated at Lawkhowa SHC, Kaliabor SDCH, TMCH, Tezpur and NMCH, Nagaon. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever with body pain and cough were reported from Village Tarwadih, Sub-District Latehar, District Latehar. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. Both children and adults were affected. Blood samples were collected from all cases for microscopy peripheral blood smear (MP) and Widal test, 1 sample was positive for Malaria Falciparum. Anti-malaria drugs were provided by the medical team. Antibiotics and other medicines were provided to the rest of the persons who were suffering from fever and cough. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of fever with body pain, headache and myalgia were reported from Village Thrikkakkara North, Sub-District Kanayannur, District Ernakulam. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house fever survey was done. The affected age group was 19-38 years. Cases were treated at PHC Kalamassery,FHC Cheranalloor. Out of 12 Blood samples collected, 11 samples tested positive for Dengue (NS1 Ag Elisa). Fogging and source reduction activities were carried out. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on vector control measures, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of vomiting, loss of appetite, and yellow discolouration of eyes and urine were reported from Sub-District Thalassery, District Kannur. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 1 to 15 years. House-to-house survey was done. Cases were treated at UPHC Koothuparamba. 22 water samples were collected and tested at KWA Koothuparamba for bacteriological analysis. Of these, 15 samples tested positive for E. coli and coliforms. No blood samples were collected. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of vomiting, loss of appetite, and yellow discolouration of eyes and urine were reported from Sub-District Thalassery, District Kannur. District RRT investigated the outbreak. The affected age group was 6 to 60 years. A house- to-house survey was done. Cases were treated at UPHC Chittariparamba. 5 blood samples were collected and tested at PHC Chittariparamba using the HAV IgM card test, of which 1 sample tested positive. 1 serum sample was sent to RPH Lab, Kannur, for HAV IgM ELISA testing, and the result was positive. Community awareness and health education were given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.
